transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (SE), Rita (CSM); Priya (Evercrest Head of ML), Carlos (Platform), Lena (FinOps)

Summary:
Brief health check focused on usage trends, unexpected cost variance in September, and proposed mitigations (dedicated capacity vs routing policies). Agreed to run targeted KV-cache / batching tests using customer traces, share security artifacts, and plan a VPC deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Usage and spike analysis (September surge)
- Cost drivers: tail latencies, small-batch penalties, embedding reruns
- Reliability: error surface, 95th/99th p99 behavior over last 30 days
- Roadmap: pilot timeline for Dedicated pool and VPC onboarding
- Security/compliance checkpoints (KMS, audit logs, SSO)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, going to kick off. hows everybodys day?
[00:07] Priya: good, thanks. we had a rough friday — traffic spiked from a campaign so wanted to get alignment on cost and latency.
[00:15] Jonas: yeah we saw the traces you sent, there was a lot of short-lived chat calls with high prefix reuse but poor cache hits in the last 2 weeks, so effective batching dropped.
[00:28] Carlos: quick question, when you say 'cache hits' can you explain like layman for our product folks? i think we might be mis-configuring the prefix keys.
[00:36] Jonas: sure — so KV cache stores past key/value attention states per session. when session prefixes are identical across requests we can reuse the cache, avoid recomputing. if tokens differ slightly, hits degrade. sometimes our client sdk keys are ephemeral, so that hurts hit rate.
[00:50] Priya: right that's likely what happened — we rolled a client change that adds trace ids into the prompt, which probably broke cache grouping.
[00:58] Rita: ok noted, that explains the tiny-batch penalty. lena — can you share a bit on the cost surprise from finops side?
[01:05] Lena: sure, so September was about 37% higher unit cost than our forecast; the finance team flagged the delta. main contributors appear to be more generation tokens per request and a 3x increase in retry calls when model returned partial outputs.
[01:20] Maya: retries are interesting — are these user retries or automatic client retries?
[01:24] Carlos: a mix. some are UX retries, others are timeouts in our edge layer that re-sent the request because p99 got past our 1.2s threshold.
[01:33] Jonas: that's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff — to avoid tail we see orchestration re-tries or bigger timeout windows. one lever is dedicated capacity to reduce tail variability; another is smarter routing and backoff.
[01:45] Priya: we wanted to understand the economics though — dedicated pool costs upfront. is there a good breakeven point for us?
[01:52] Maya: yes, we can model that. based on your spike profile and the percent of small-batch/short seq requests, dedicated becomes cheaper at sustained high qps with predictable diurnal patterns. we should run the sim against your traces.
[02:06] (slight crosstalk)
[02:10] Jonas: also quantization profiles matter — some of your workloads can run a quantized variant with negligible quality drop which gives 25-40% throughput improvement. we can recommend models to try.
[02:21] Priya: any risk to quality? our NLU accuracy is sensitive to hallucination on slot-filling tasks.
[02:27] Jonas: we won't guess — we'll A/B with small holdouts. if we see regressed F1 we'll roll back. Redwood Optimize gives per-prompt eval hooks so you can monitor.
[02:40] Lena: on security — finance asked if host keys and transcripts are encrypted end-to-end, and whether we can keep logs within our VPC.
[02:48] Maya: yes — with Private you get customer-managed KMS and option for on-prem or VPC routing. audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM, and we have SOC2 Type II evidence — i'll share the docs.
[02:59] Priya: perfect, and what about RBAC? we need separation between our ML team and data science contractors.
[03:06] Rita: we have token-level RBAC and IAM integrations (SAML/SSO). role scoping can be set per-route and we can audit token usage in the console.
[03:17] Carlos: ok that addresses compliance. back to the cost — you mentioned batching; what exactly will Jonas run with our traces?
[03:24] Jonas: i'll run two experiments: 1) simulated continuous batching with your inter-arrival times to estimate effective batch size vs latency; 2) KV-cache sensitivity by normalizing prefixes to see potential hit rate gains if you remove ephemeral IDs. both are quick runs but need the raw traces.
[03:38] Priya: we'll sanitize and send three traces: baseline, peak, and campaign spike. expect those by end of monday.
[03:45] Maya: great. once we run that, we'll produce a short cost delta projection comparing hosted vs small Dedicated pool vs Dedicated with quantized model.
[03:56] (sound of paper shuffling)
[04:01] Lena: finance also needs a projection of month-over-month burn if we enable autoscaling burst. we prefer capped burst but with alerts.
[04:10] Maya: we can propose a policy: primary dedicated pool for steady throughput + burst routed to hosted with cost caps and auto-fallover. that gives reliability while limiting spend.
[04:22] Priya: any notes on latency SLOs? we need p95 <= 700ms for our checkout flow.
[04:28] Jonas: p95 700ms is achievable on Dedicated in-region with optimized kernels and continuous batching, but p99 will depend on sequence length variability. for checkout, keep sequences under 256 tokens and use prefix caching where possible.
[04:43] Maya: that's an implementation ask for the app team — Priya, can your engineers enforce input truncation and canonical prefixes?
[04:50] Priya: yes we'll scope that work, likely 2 sprints.
[04:54] Carlos: timeline question — how long to pilot Dedicated with VPC routing?
[04:59] Rita: typical private pilot (VPC peering + small pool) is 3-4 weeks for initial onboarding, longer if you want HSM/KMS integration.
[05:08] Lena: budget wants a firm estimate before committing.
[05:11] Maya: i'll send the cost model matrix — three scenarios: hosted only, reserved small Dedicated (8 GPUs), Dedicated + quantized. we'll show expected unit cost and time-to-breakeven.
[05:22] (brief pause)
[05:27] Priya: one more technical: our edge retries are sometimes invisible in traces because we rewrite headers. can you recommend instrumentation?
[05:35] Jonas: add a stable session id header before any client middleware touches it. that will preserve prefix grouping and let cache work. also enable per-request debug flags in sandbox to trace KV hits.
[05:47] Carlos: will do.
[05:49] Rita: ok to recap and next steps?
[05:52] Maya: recap: customer to send traces; Jonas to run batching and KV experiments; Maya to share security pack and cost matrix; schedule VPC deep-dive next week (2 hours). action items in the notes.
[06:07] Priya: sounds good. thank you everyone.
[06:10] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites and the docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels approximate; there were a few overlapped segments and some jargon got transcribed imprecisely (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes as 'K V cash', 'quantization' as 'quan tization').
